extracted.intended_audience: researchers and graduate students in educational psychology / learning sciences studying self-regulated learning (SRL)
extracted.subtask_description: Comparative review and evaluation of theoretical SRL models (e.g., Winne & Hadwin, Pintrich, Efklides, Hadwin et al.) covering their phases, subprocesses, emphases (metacognition, motivation, emotion), empirical support, and measurement approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical evidence / model validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the model have empirical support? (e.g., Greene and Azevedo reviewed 113 studies supporting Winne & Hadwin; other models have varying degrees of direct empirical validation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate quantity and scope of empirical studies, whether reviews are comprehensive, whether empirical work addresses all model aspects (including extensions like emotion), and heed author-noted gaps (e.g., clarify long-term SRL changes, phase four/external evaluations, incorporate motivation regulation, development across the lifespan, effects of student characteristics such as learning disabilities).

rubrics_metrics.name: Instruments and measurement methods (trace data, scaﬀolding tools)
rubrics_metrics.description: Availability and use of measurement tools based on the model, especially computer-supported environments that scaffold SRL while recording trace/log data (e.g., nStudy and gStudy for Winne’s framework).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the model inspired objective online/’on-the-fly’ measures, use of trace data for temporal/sequential analyses, and whether measurement approaches enable fine-grained temporal study of SRL (Winne et al.; Winne & Perry emphasis on online SRL measures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability and validation of questionnaires (MSLQ and related scales)
rubrics_metrics.description: Existence and psychometric support of standardized questionnaires tied to the model (e.g., Pintrich’s MSLQ: 15 scales; motivation section 31 items; learning strategies 50 items subdivided into cognitive, metacognitive, resource management).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess instrument strengths (e.g., combination of SRL and motivation, versions for college and high school), prevalence of use in the literature, and reviews reporting its widespread adoption (Roth et al., Honicke & Broadbent).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of regulation areas (cognition, motivation/affect, behavior, context)
rubrics_metrics.description: Which areas of regulation the model explicitly includes — for example Pintrich’s four areas: cognition, motivation/aﬀect, behavior, and context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare whether models include regulation of overt behavior and context (unique to Pintrich), and how comprehensively each area is operationalized (e.g., specific subprocesses like self-observations, efficacy judgments, context monitoring).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-level structure (Person/macro vs Task × Person/micro)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the model posits multiple interacting levels such as Efklides’ MASRL distinction between a Person (macro) level and a Task × Person (micro) level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate top–down (goal-driven person-level processes) versus bottom–up (data-driven task-level metacognitive activity), the functions assigned to each level (e.g., macro: self-concept, motivation; micro: moment-to-moment monitoring, affect regulation), and empirical claims required (identify two levels, task effects, and interactions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Metacognition–aﬀect–motivation interaction (theoretical clarity)
rubrics_metrics.description: How clearly and explicitly the model describes interactions among metacognition, motivation, and aﬀect (Efklides’ MASRL emphasizes these interactions and specifies empirical tenets to be tested).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for explicit hypotheses the model poses (Efklides’ three tenets: identifying two levels and their interactions, interaction of motivation and aﬀect across levels, different forms of metacognition at each level) and whether the literature provides supporting studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social regulation modes in collaborative settings (SRL, CoRL, SSRL)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether and how the model addresses regulation in social/collaborative learning, including distinct modes: individual self-regulation (SRL), co-regulation (CoRL), and shared regulation (SSRL) (Hadwin et al.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess clarity of definitions (CoRL: affordances/constraints and directed guidance; SSRL: deliberate transactive planning and jointly negotiated regulation), consistency of usage in the field, and empirical reconceptualizations (e.g., CoRL/SSRL often co-occur across collaboration phases).

rubrics_metrics.name: Group regulatory process architecture (feedback loops / phases in SSRL)
rubrics_metrics.description: The process structure for group regulation (Hadwin et al.: four loosely sequenced, recursively linked feedback loops: negotiate shared task perceptions; set shared goals and plans; coordinate/monitor and adapt; evaluate and regulate for future performance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the model provides distinct loops/phases for group activity, how these map to individual SRL phases, and evidence that groups progress through or mix these loops in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation of COPES architecture / computational clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the model integrates Winne’s COPES (Conditions, Operations, Products, Evaluations, Standards) architecture to clarify (meta)cognitive processing (Hadwin et al. forthcoming integration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether inclusion of COPES enhances specificity of information-processing assumptions, links to observable operations, and facilitates measurement/analysis of metacognitive processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of multimodal, context-aware instrumentation for SSRL
rubrics_metrics.description: Adoption of multimodal measures (eye-tracking, physiological responses) combined with subjective data and CSCL tools to measure and scaffold SSRL in context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appraise whether instruments capture contextual interactions, triangulate objective and subjective measures, and allow investigation of social/regulatory processes in situ (e.g., CSCL environments that promote awareness, planning, evaluation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Citations and perceived importance (bibliometric indicator)
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of citations of a model’s main publication as an indicator of influence (table comparing citation counts per model provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use citation counts cautiously: they can reflect factors beyond theoretical quality (age, accessibility, field use); the review compares raw totals and citations per year while noting caveats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phases and subprocesses (preparatory, performance, appraisal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the model maps SRL into preparatory/forethought, performance, and appraisal/reflection phases and which subprocesses are identified within each phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare models that present clearly delimited phases with subprocesses (Pintrich, Zimmerman) vs. models that present open/recursive feedback loops (Winne & Hadwin, Boekaerts, Efklides, SSRL), and consider implications for measurability and intervention specificity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree of emphasis on (meta)cognition
rubrics_metrics.description: How central metacognition is in the model (three-level classification: e.g., Winne & Hadwin and Efklides strongly metacognitive; Pintrich and Zimmerman emphasize metacognitive strategies but alongside motivation; Boekaerts less explicit about specific strategies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the model treats metacognitive monitoring as the gateway to SRL, details metacognitive subprocesses, and provides operationalizable constructs for measurement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree of emphasis on motivation
rubrics_metrics.description: How strongly the model foregrounds motivation (two-level classification: Zimmerman, Boekaerts, Pintrich at first level; SSRL, Efklides, Winne at second level).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate where motivation appears in phase structures (e.g., forethought self-motivation beliefs in Zimmerman), whether motivational components are differentiated (goal orientation, self-efficacy), and how motivation is linked to SRL outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree of emphasis on emotion / emotion-regulation
rubrics_metrics.description: How explicitly emotion and emotion-regulation are integrated (three-level classification: Boekaerts strongly emphasizes emotions and divergent goal pathways; Pintrich/Zimmerman focus on affective reactions in self-reflection; others vary).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether models specify emotion-regulation strategies, pathways (learning vs well-being), and empirical work on emotional challenges (especially in collaborative contexts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conceptualization style: distinct phases vs open/recursive process
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the model conceptualizes SRL as discrete phases with distinct subprocesses (Zimmerman, Pintrich) or as an open recursive feedback loop with less phase delimitation (Winne & Hadwin, Boekaerts, Efklides, SSRL forthcoming).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider consequences for intervention design: phase-distinct models may allow more targeted interventions and measurement, while open-process models may suggest more holistic interventions; empirical testing required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence or absence of classical measurement instruments for model
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether classical (paper/online questionnaires) instruments have been built specifically from the model (e.g., Pintrich’s MSLQ exists; Winne & Hadwin historically lacked classical instruments but have scaffolded computer environments; SSRL lacks classical questionnaires but uses contextual measures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the fit between model concepts and available instruments, noting where model authors developed tools (questionnaires, metacognitive experiences questionnaires) or where novel methodologies are needed (multi-modal/contextual measures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal and sequential analysis opportunities (trace data advantage)
rubrics_metrics.description: The model’s suitability for temporal/sequential analysis of SRL via trace/log data (Winne’s earlier work opened possibilities for temporal/sequential analysis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor models and associated tools that permit fine-grained temporal analyses of SRL processes (enabling research into dynamic, time-ordered regulatory activity).
